Horsehead Corporation, historically headquartered at **300 Frankfort Road in Monaca, Pennsylvania**, stands as a landmark name in the American metallurgical and industrial chemical sectors. For much of the 20th and early 21st centuries, the company was recognized as the leading producer of zinc metal and zinc-based chemicals in the United States. What set Horsehead apart from traditional mining entities was its pioneering role in the "circular economy" long before the term became a corporate mainstay. The company specialized in the recycling of Electric Arc Furnace (EAF) dust—a hazardous byproduct generated by the steel-making industry—transforming what would otherwise be environmental waste into valuable industrial commodities.

The Monaca facility served as the operational nerve center for these complex processes. Utilizing proprietary Waelz kiln technology, Horsehead extracted zinc from industrial waste to produce a diverse portfolio of products, including zinc oxide, zinc dust, and high-purity zinc metal. These materials are essential components in a vast array of everyday applications, from the vulcanization of rubber for tires and the production of sunscreens to the manufacturing of ceramics, paints, and agricultural fertilizers. By reclaiming these minerals, Horsehead provided a critical service to the domestic steel industry while reducing the demand for primary mining.

The site at 300 Frankfort Road is deeply woven into the industrial fabric of Beaver County. Over the decades, the corporation (which previously operated under the name Zinc Corporation of America) was one of the largest employers in the region, sustaining generations of local families. However, the company faced a period of significant transition in 2016, leading to a Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing and a subsequent acquisition and rebranding as American Zinc Recycling (AZR). 

Today, the legacy of the Horsehead Corporation at the Monaca site is most notably linked to the shifting energy landscape; the massive industrial footprint formerly occupied by Horsehead was eventually cleared to make way for the Shell Polymers Monaca petrochemical complex (the "cracker plant"). While the skyline at 300 Frankfort Road has changed, the history of Horsehead Corporation remains a vital chapter in Pennsylvania’s manufacturing heritage, representing a century of innovation in chemical recycling and mineral processing.
